senses.gloss:
Ahalyā
------------------------------------------
Ahalyā, the wife of the sage गौतम and मोथेर् of another sage Śatānanda, is a well-known character in Hindu म्य्थोलोग्य्. She is said to have been born out of creator ब्रह्मा’s मिन्द् as the very personification of feminine grace and beauty and given in मर्रिअगे to the महर्षि गौतम. Infatuated by her beauty, इन्द्र the king of gods impersonated गौतम and seduced her. Consequently she was cursed by the sage गौतम to remain invisible for a thousand years sustaining herself only on air and wallowing in ash. She was redeemed by राम, the son of दशरथ and restored to गौतम.
Some works like the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa say that she was converted into a stone. This version seems to be more popular.
When Uttaṅka (or उदङ्क), a disciple of गौतम, offered to fulfil any of her desires as his गुरुदक्षिणा (fees due to the preceptor) she asked for the kuṇḍalas (ear-ornaments) of queen Madayantī (wife of the king Saudāsa). Uttaṅka secured them successfully, though with great difficulty.
See also GAUTAMA.

āhāva
(‘calling’)
------------------------------------------
Derived from the root ‘hve’ (‘to call’) आहाव is the technical name of a formula of summons pronounced loudly by the होतृ (chief of the priests representing the Ṛgveda) in a सोम sacrifice before starting the शस्त्र (laudatory recitation). It is usually in the form of: śoṁ 3 1 sāvom or śoṁsāvo 3 (a corrupt form of śaṁsāva).
Soma juice is extracted (savana) three times during the day: morning (prāta-ssavana), noon (mādhyandinasavana) and later in the day (tṛtīyasavana). During all these three savanas आहाव is done 4 times in the first, 5 times in the second and again 4 times in the third.
The formula of reply by the अध्वर्यु (chief of the priests representing the Yajurveda) is called प्रतिगर.
See also PRATIGARA and ŚASTRA.

āhārya
(‘that which is brought’)
------------------------------------------
During वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्, the first fire is normally produced by churning the araṇis (See ARAṆI for details.). Subsequent fires can be generated by taking the embers from the fire that is already lighted, like the गार्हपत्य. Such fire ‘that is brought’ is called आहार्य.

ahaṅkāra
(‘egoism’)
------------------------------------------
Ahaṅkāra is that which produces abhimāna, the sense of ‘I’ and ‘mine.’ According to Sāṅkhyan metaphysics, a large part of which is accepted by Vedānta, अहङ्कार is the principle of individuation that arises after महत् or बुद्धि in the process of evolution from प्रकृति (nature). It is regarded as a substance since it is the material cause of other substances like the मिन्द् or the sense-organs. Through its action the different puruṣas (individual selves) become endowed each with a separate mental background. These puruṣas identify themselves with the acts of प्रकृति through अहङ्कार.
At the individual level it makes the पुरुष feel that he is receiving the sensations through the senses and the मिन्द्, and deciding about appropriate action, through the intellect.
At the cosmic level, the five senses of चोग्नितिओन् (jñānendriyas), the five organs of action (karmendriyas), the मिन्द् (manas) and the five subtle elements like the earth (tanmātras) are produced out of अहङ्कार.
In some works of Vedānta, अहङ्कार is considered as a function of अन्तःकरण (internal instrument or मिन्द्), responsible for ego-sense and possessiveness.
Ahaṅkāra as egoism or self-conceit is considered as a great obstacle in spiritual life and the cultivation of humility is prescribed as its antidote.
See also SĀṄKHYA DARŚANA.

Ahalyābāī Hoḷkar
(A. D. 1735-1795)
------------------------------------------
One of the few Hindu rulers of the medieval period, who did much for the protection of हिन्दुइस्म् and preservation of हिन्दु तेम्प्लेस् was अहल्याबाई होऌकर्, the queen of Indore.
Though born in a poor family of farmers, she was married to Khaṇḍe Rāo, the son of Mallhār Rāo Hoḷkar of Indore. When her husband died in a battle, she boldly took over the administration in A.D. 1765 and ruled with great efficiency till her demise in A. D. 1795. She was responsible for the protection of the original Śivaliṅgas of Somanātha and काशी temples by building separate temples for the same. She improved or renovated many temples in North India and also built rest-houses for pilgrims in the places of पिल्ग्रिमगे. The modern city of Indore owes its development mainly to her.

āhavanīya
(‘to be offered as an oblation’)
------------------------------------------
Anyone who establishes the Vedic fires normally maintains three fires: गार्हपत्य, आहवनीय and दक्षिणाग्नि. Most of the special sacrifices are performed in the आहवनीय which is kindled by the fire brought from the गार्हपत्य.
The mound of आहवनीय is square and is situated on the eastern side of the sacrificial shed at a distance of twenty four padas or steps from the गार्हपत्य mound.
The fire is established at dawn when half of the sun’s disc has risen above the horizon. The अध्वर्यु lights a few fuel sticks on the गार्हपत्य fire and carries them in a vessel containing sand to the आहवनीय mound chanting the appropriate mantras. After establishing the fire it is propitiated with oblations of clarified butter and fuel sticks.
In case the fire goes out, prescribed prāyaścittas or expiations should be under-gone. Reverencing it before death is believed to confer celestial worlds on the sacrificer.
See also PAÑCĀGNI.

āhāraśuddhi
(‘purity of ड़ोओद्’)
------------------------------------------
Hindu scriptural works declare that there is a close relationship between the body and the मिन्द्. In fact it is the मिन्द्, as the repository of कर्म, that creates the future body since it survives the death of the physical bodies till the attainment of मोक्ष (liberation). Hence the body and the मिन्द् act and react on each other. In this context आहार or ड़ोओद् assumes great importance. The quality of ड़ोओद् affects the quality of मिन्द्. In fact the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (7.26.2) goes to the extent of declaring that purity of ड़ोओद् leads to purity of मिन्द् which results in the excellent retention in memory of all that is heard and studied from the preceptor. The resultant wisdom leads to freedom from all bonds. This is because the subtle part of the ड़ोओद् that is eaten sustains the मिन्द् whereas the gross part of it nourishes the body.
Āhāra is classified into three groups:
sāttvika, rājasika and tāmasika (vide Bhagavadgītā 17.7-10). Sāttvika ड़ोओद् contributes to longevity, health, strength and happiness. Rājasika ड़ोओद् generates passion leading to sorrow and suffering. Tāmasika ड़ोओद् produces dullness, indolence and drownsiness.
The various scriptural works mention long lists of ड़ोओद् articles coming under these three categories.
There are regulations with regard to the quantity of ड़ोओद् to be eaten and elaborate rules regarding the time, place and also company in which it should be taken.
Moderation in eating is always the rule. Hindu medical works recommend that half the stomach should be filled with solid ड़ोओद् and a quarter with water leaving the rest of the space for the movement of air.
One is advised to avoid partaking of ड़ोओद् before performing spiritual practices. Solar and lunar eclipses are believed to have very adverse effects on ड़ोओद् and hence one should not eat during eclipses.
Places to be avoided for eating include temples, public places, moving animals and vehicles.
Impurity (doṣa) can accrue to ड़ोओद् on three counts: jātidoṣa, nimittadoṣa and āśrayadoṣa. Garlic or cabbage for instance, is impure by its very species (jāti) and hence must be avoided. Nimittadoṣa comes by external impurities like dust or hair as also an insanitary handling of ड़ोओद्. This can be obviated by strictly observing the rules of health and sanitation. Foods cooked, touched or handled by persons of questionable character become contaminated by their evil psychic vibrations which can be transmitted to those who consume them. This type of impurity is called āśrayadoṣa, दोष or defect arising as a result of āśraya or repository. Offering the ड़ोओद् to God before eating destroys this impurity.
